subject: BYOK carveout + SSO connector prioritization
messages:
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai, procurement@healthspring.com
Cc: security@clearwell.io
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: BYOK carveout + SSO connector prioritization

Hi all,

Looping you in to triage HealthSpring's ask and decide where this lives on the roadmap. High level: HealthSpring needs temporary BYOK (short-lived keys) for a pilot, tighter SSO connector control (attribute mapping + SCIM sync), and audit evidence for a 30-day retention window. Their procurement team also called out FIPS-validated KMS for escrow scenarios.

Questions we need to resolve this week:
- Product: can we expose a temporary BYOK \"ephemeral key\" mode (TTL + auto-rotation) that surfaces in Console and audit logs?
- Infra/Ops: what's the minimum KMS change to support FIPS-backed escrow for a customer carveout?
- Identity: will the SSO connector require custom IdP mapping for HealthSpring's attributes, and can SCIM be enabled during canary?
- Evidence: what audit log granularity can we provide for token-level actions vs. system-level?

Attachments: evidence_matrix.xlsx (current evidence template), sso-config.diff (proposal for IDP mapping knobs).

Proposed immediate plan:
1) Quick sync (30 min) this Thursday to agree owners and P0/P1 split.
2) Product to spec the ephemeral BYOK API and retention config by EOD 2027-09-16.
3) Infra to prototype SSO connector with SCIM off-by-default and a canary path for HealthSpring by 2027-09-30.
4) Legal/procurement to confirm acceptable escrow options (FIPS-only?) and sign off.

If we treat this as P0 for private deployments and P1 for hosted, we can limit blast radius and surface a clear path for HealthSpring's pilot.

Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Security Program Manager | Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwood.ai

---
Attachments: evidence_matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet stub), sso-config.diff (unified diff stub)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai, procurement@healthspring.com
Date: Tue, 7 Sep 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BYOK carveout + SSO connector prioritization

Naomi — thanks for pulling this together. A few technical constraints / clarifying notes: 

- SSO connector: HealthSpring's IdP requires mapped attributes (employee_id, role, org_unit). We can add mapping knobs but SCIM provisioning introduces a separate auth path (we should keep SCIM off in canary).
- KMS: supporting FIPS-backed escrow is non-trivial; requires us to provision a separate key ring with FIPS HSM backing or partner with a FIPS-compliant provider. Ops estimate ~4-6 weeks for a minimal proof-of-concept (non-blocking if we offer hosted fallback).
- Retention/audit: current runtime can emit token-level events but retention windows are coarse (30/90/365). To present 30-day evidence with per-token granularity we need a short retention tier in the telemetry pipeline and an evidence-extraction job (SEC-2141).

Suggested split:
- P0: Ephemeral BYOK API + Console controls for private deployments (owner: product, timeline: spec 9/16, API impl 10/14).
- P1: Hosted fallback + marketplace ops (owner: infra + commercial).

I'll add SEC-2141 to track the audit pipeline changes; product should link to that ticket. Quick ask: can Product confirm whether the ephemeral key TTL can be set to 1h/12h/7d? That affects caching & KV behaviour.

On Thu 09/09 I'm available 10:00-10:45 for the 30-min sync.

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Engineering Manager, Security Platform

From: Maya Singh <maya.singh@healthspring.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@healthspring.com
Date: Wed, 8 Sep 2027 14:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BYOK carveout + SSO connector prioritization

Thanks Naomi — appreciate the clear list. A couple of constraints from our side that should inform prioritization:

- Procurement requires 30-day retention evidence in the form of exported logs (individual token events) during the pilot window. We can accept a compressed CSV export if the fields match the evidence matrix.
- On escrow: HealthSpring policy requires FIPS-validated KMS for any escrowed keys. We cannot accept a non-FIPS escrow. If Redwood can offer an HSM-backed ring or a FIPS partner for escrow, we can proceed.
- SSO: mapping is critical; our HRIS only exposes employee_id and department. SCIM would be preferred for provisioning but we can accept a manual mapping during the pilot if SCIM is gated.

Attached: HS_compliance_requirements.pdf (procurement's short checklist).

We are aiming for a pilot start in mid-October. If Redwood can deliver the ephemeral BYOK + exportable 30-day evidence path, procurement will greenlight the pilot and speed up contract. Let us know if FIPS is a hard blocker — we can discuss a transitional agreement if product/infra can commit to a timeline.

Best,
Maya Singh
Senior Security Engineer, HealthSpring
maya.singh@healthspring.com

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai, logan_wright@redwood.ai, maya.singh@healthspring.com, procurement@healthspring.com
Date: Thu, 9 Sep 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: BYOK carveout + SSO connector prioritization — decisions and owners

Thanks everyone — quick summary and owners so this doesn't fall through the cracks: 

Decisions made:
- Scope: Treat as P0 for private deployments (HealthSpring pilot), P1 for hosted.
- Ephemeral BYOK: Product to spec an API that supports TTLs (1h, 12h, 7d) and a \"canary\" mode flag visible in Console.
- Audit evidence: We will provide an exportable CSV for 30-day retention via a short-retention telemetry tier and an extraction job (track in SEC-2141).
- Escrow / FIPS: Escrow will require FIPS-backed KMS; Ops will evaluate partner options and report back. No escrow until FIPS option confirmed.

Owners & deadlines:
- Product (Marissa): Spec ephemeral BYOK + Console controls by 2027-09-16. Link your spec to SEC-2141.
- Infra/Ops (Jonas & Logan): Spike partner FIPS options and estimate for HSM-backed key ring by 2027-09-23. Prototype SSO connector canary path by 2027-09-30.
- Security Program (Naomi): Coordinate evidence template with HealthSpring and validate CSV export fields by 2027-09-16.
- Legal/Procurement (Priyom): Draft transitional clause for pilot if FIPS will not be ready by pilot start, due 2027-09-21.

Follow-ups:
- I've scheduled the 30-min sync for Thu 09/09 at 10:15 PST — meeting invite sent separately.
- Jonas: please add SEC-2141 acceptance criteria and link to the evidence_matrix.xlsx.

If anyone can't meet the deadlines above, call it out in the next 24h and we'll re-prioritize.

Thanks — Naomi
Naomi Feldman
